comparison: Perfect agreement on IBTK-eIF4A interaction data (C3, C40-C47). Both evaluations find the evidence compelling and well-supported through multiple orthogonal approaches (AP-MS, BioID, co-IP). OpenEval and peer reviewers both emphasize the specificity for eIF4A family members and the strength of convergent methodologies.

Strong agreement on non-degradative ubiquitination of eIF4A1 (C4, C50-C71). Both evaluations accept the ubiquitination characterization as compelling. OpenEval includes claims C57, C66 not mentioned in peer review, but both conclude the evidence for multi-mono-ubiquitination is well-established through in vivo, in vitro, and mass spectrometry data.

Divergent evaluations on translation inhibition effects (C5, C6, C72-C85). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with strong evidence from multiple assays. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, requesting clarification on whether eIF4A1 overexpression can rescue phenotypes and whether IBTK has additional targets beyond eIF4A1. OpenEval includes stress granule data (C77-C80) not mentioned in peer review.

Both identify concerns about post-transcriptional regulation mechanism (C7, C87-C92). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes complexity when eIF4A1 overexpression cannot rescue. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, highlighting that several eIF4A1 target oncogenes remain unchanged and questioning the completeness of the mechanism.

Agreement on oncogenic role and tumor-suppressive effects of IBTK depletion (C8, C93-C100, C142). Both evaluations accept the functional cancer phenotype data as well-supported through in vitro and in vivo experiments. OpenEval emphasizes comprehensive phenotypic characterization; peer reviewers note clinical data linking IBTK to poor prognosis strengthens findings.

Significant disagreement on mTORC1/S6K1 phosphorylation of IBTK (C9, C10, C108-C126). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED despite noting only 4 of 7 sites confirmed as direct. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN with multiple technical concerns about Phos-tag gel experiments, requests for additional controls (torin, lambda phosphatase), and confusion about band patterns in starvation experiments.

Agreement on functional importance of IBTK phosphorylation (C127-C134). Both evaluations accept that the phosphorylation-deficient mutant (7S/TA) demonstrates functional consequences linking mTORC1/S6K1 to IBTK's oncogenic functions. Despite peer concerns about phosphorylation mapping (R6), the functional data with the mutant are not challenged.

Agreement on immune-related effects through eIF4F-STAT1-IRF1-PD-L1 pathway (C101-C107). Both evaluations accept the immune infiltration and PD-L1 data as supporting IBTK's role in tumor immune evasion. OpenEval emphasizes mechanistic link and use of immunocompetent mice; peer reviewers note this strengthens overall findings without raising concerns.

Perfect agreement on clinical relevance (C135-C139). Both evaluations accept TCGA data and IHC validation showing IBTK correlation with pathological grade and survival. OpenEval notes adequate sample size (117 CESC tissues, 35 normal); peer reviewers cite clinical data as supporting functional importance.

OpenEval identifies literature-based background claims (C1, C2, C11-C39, C48-C49, C61-C63, C66, C86, C141) as SUPPORTED context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these are established prior work rather than novel findings requiring peer assessment.

OpenEval rates therapeutic potential claims (C140, C142, C143) as UNCERTAIN, noting they are speculative hypotheses requiring additional validation. While C142 (sensitization to eIF4A inhibitors) appears in peer R5 as accepted data, the broader therapeutic implications are not explicitly evaluated by peer reviewers.
